motivo: Todas las cifras (23 personas 50,7%; 40 personas 89,1%; 70 personas 99,9%; 253 pares) coinciden con Wikipedia 'Birthday problem' y MathWorld 'Birthday Problem' (0.507297). La nota sobre cumpleaños no uniformes (aumenta la probabilidad) esta respaldada por Wikipedia y MathWorld. No hay afirmaciones de salud, seguridad ni plata, ni anecdotas dudosas, ni falsas. Las fuentes citadas respaldan lo atribuido.

afirmaciones.texto: Twenty-three people are enough for the odds of a shared birthday to exceed fifty percent (caption: about 50.7%)
Twenty-three people make two hundred fifty-three pairs (23 x 22 / 2)
Forty people: about ninety percent (caption: about 89%)
The math assumes every day is equally likely; real birthdays are not evenly spread
afirmaciones.fuente: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthday_problem; https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BirthdayProblem.html (more than 6% above average in September in the US)

afirmaciones.texto: Uneven birthdays nudge the odds up (make a match slightly more likely, not less)
afirmaciones.fuente: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthday_problem ('Any unevenness increases the likelihood of two people sharing a birthday'; not enough to change the 23 threshold)

afirmaciones.texto: Any two people in the room count, not only you (the match is between any pair)
afirmaciones.fuente: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birthday_problem (definicion del problema: any two of n people)

afirmaciones.texto: It's the number of pairs, not people, that matters (mecanismo)
Caption: 'Sources: Wikipedia, Birthday problem' respalda las cifras citadas
